title: Ambient alpha-compact triangulated class in a Grothendieck derived category
statement: For an essentially v-small class P in D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with coproducts [lem-grothendieck-derived-has-coproducts], choose a regular alpha and an essentially v-small replete triangulated class S containing P, closed under fewer-than-alpha coproducts, and equal to the canonical alpha-compact class [def-sfb-alpha-compact-object].

source.place: Ambient well-generation and common cardinal bound: Neeman Theorem 0.2; Krause Localization theory Sections 6.2-6.3.

proof.text: Unpack the alpha-compact core theorem and use its exact class characterization and the ranks of P to obtain P at most S.

statement_change.old_statement: For an essentially v-small class P in the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category, there are an object property S and a regular cardinal alpha in universe v such that S is essentially v-small, replete and triangulated, contains P, is closed under coproducts indexed by types of cardinality less than alpha, and every object of S is alpha-presentable.
statement_change.what: The source defines alpha-compactness by alpha-smallness and coproduct factorization G4, not ordinary IsCardinalPresentable in the triangulated category. The old ordinary-presentable theorem is not established by this repair; replace that erroneous interface by the actual source notion, with all consumers adapted in the same delivery. This restores the source proof without weakening the unchanged final perfect-class theorem. Record equality with the canonical class rather than one-way membership, because Properties must transport G4 factor objects back into S.

source.place: Krause (2001) pages 121--125, alpha-small objects and maximal G4 class; Localization theory 6.3 and 6.10.2 distinguish this from presentability in the abelianization.

old_proof.text: Apply the alpha-compact class core theorem to obtain S and a regular cardinal α. Its equivalence identifies S with α-presentable objects, while its remaining clauses provide essential smallness, repleteness, triangulated closure and closure under coproducts of fewer than α summands. The final clause gives P ≤ S because every object of P is α-presentable.
